review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the repeated-proof candidates. Two have enough support. (1) `sum_cubeFlip` and `sum_cubeToggle` have the same `Finset.sum_bij` argument for an involution. (2) `majority_exists` and `majorityBit_count` have the same 'count g + count (!g) = 48' argument. `majority_exists` is not used anywhere else in this file. I did not report the smaller duplicates: `pairedEquations_acceptedCount`/`pairedEquations_failureCount`, the `cases … <;> norm_num [bitSign]` blocks, `count_union_le`/`count_remove`, and the three induction proofs over `cloneList`. These are short or only loosely similar. The same two duplications also appear in sibling files such as MaxCut/PCP/Folding.lean and BinPacking/Reductions/CloneGap.lean, so a fix could go in a shared module. I did not assess that. I could not compile any replacement, so the Lean snippets below are unchecked. `Equiv.prod_comp` is in Mathlib and `Equiv.sum_comp` is its to_additive form. `Function.Involutive.toPerm` is used elsewhere in Mathlib, for example in Cardinal/Arithmetic.lean.

findings.problem: Both lemmas prove that a sum over `Cube I` is unchanged under an involution of `Cube I`. They use the same four-goal `Finset.sum_bij` proof: membership in `univ`, injectivity via `congrArg` and the involution law, surjectivity via the preimage `σ g`, and `rfl`. The involution is the only thing that changes (`cubeFlip` vs `cubeToggle i`). Any further involution would need another copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one general lemma and define both sums from it:

theorem sum_involutive (σ : Cube I → Cube I) (hσ : Function.Involutive σ) (F : Cube I → ℝ) :
    (∑ f, F (σ f)) = ∑ f, F f :=
  Equiv.sum_comp hσ.toPerm F

The proof sketch is that an involution is a permutation of the finite type, and sums are invariant under `Equiv`. Then use it for both:

theorem sum_cubeFlip (F : Cube I → ℝ) : (∑ f, F (cubeFlip f)) = ∑ f, F f :=
  sum_involutive cubeFlip cubeFlip_cubeFlip F

theorem sum_cubeToggle (i : I) (F : Cube I → ℝ) : (∑ f, F (cubeToggle i f)) = ∑ f, F f :=
  sum_involutive (cubeToggle i) (cubeToggle_twice i) F

The hypotheses match what the file has. `cubeFlip_cubeFlip` and `cubeToggle_twice` are the pointwise statements `σ (σ f) = f`, which is `Function.Involutive σ`. The `Fintype I` assumption is already in scope. `cubeFlip_cubeFlip` has its instances omitted, which is harmless. The downstream uses at lines 43 and 160 are unchanged.
findings.benefit: About 20 lines of duplicated bijection bookkeeping become one reusable lemma and two one-line corollaries. A reader sees that both lemmas are the same fact, namely invariance under a permutation, and a bug fix or later involution lemma needs no new bijection proof.

findings.problem: Both theorems prove that one of the two values of a Boolean predicate on `indices` has at least 24 agreeing indices out of 48. Each derives `countP g + countP (!g) = 48` with `List.length_eq_countP_add_countP`, repeats the identical `hn` rewrite of `decide (¬g i = true)` to `!g i`, and then does the same `by_cases 24 ≤ countP g` plus `omega`. `majority_exists` is the existential form and `majorityBit_count` is the explicit-witness form. `majority_exists` is not referenced elsewhere in the file. Only `majorityBit_count` is used, in `clone_gap`.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the counting argument once. Keep `majorityBit` and `majorityBit_count` (move their definitions before `majority_exists`), then derive the existential from them:

theorem majority_exists (g : Index → Bool) :
    ∃ b : Bool, 24 ≤ indices.countP (fun i => g i == b) :=
  ⟨majorityBit g, majorityBit_count g⟩

If `majority_exists` has no users, delete it instead. The `hn` rewrite and `length_eq_countP_add_countP` step then live only in `majorityBit_count`. The hypotheses are identical (`g : Index → Bool`) and only `length_indices` is needed, so no new imports are involved.
findings.benefit: This removes about 13 duplicated lines of case-splitting and arithmetic. The majority fact then has a single proof, so a change to the threshold 24 or the index count 48 is made in one place and the two statements cannot drift apart.
